items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1958-Fall
items.q: Oh, after I met Jenny, I began to look up these different jazz players

ctx.x: Well, I used to talk to him, and then, because I asked him about a lot of other musicians and all that, you know. He never talked much about himself, but he had plenty to say about Umber Simeon, for example, and Freddie Kepler and Perez. Yeah, that's right. He liked them.

Yeah, he liked them. And the funny thing about that, see, I had, I'd been pretty much out of Bud Rack time and enough. To about 1925, I'd bought a few records now and then, most with piano records. But in 1925, I started going to night school, and I was working daytime, and I didn't have time for anything else. So I dropped out of my life entirely, almost, to music. I didn't play much. My nephew came low, he was playing, and I wouldn't pay much attention. So, I started to tell something I'm going to forget. What…

I asked him about Begg Speederbeck. I said, are you familiar with him? He said, yes. I said, have you heard him play? He said, yes, I heard him play. I said, well, was he good? He said, yes, he was good. He wasn't as good as they say he was. That's about his course. He said, no, I've never heard him play. He said, yes, he was good. He said, he wasn't as good as they say.
